claims.name: below C7
claims.use: the cervicothoracic junction, where a body called cervical or thoracic decides the approach and the hardware; kept as a reference border, with no source checked here for its clinical use

claims.name: below T5
claims.use: the upper end of the T5 to T12 sagittal curve, on which the Lenke classification of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis grades its sagittal thoracic modifier (under +10, +10 to +40, over +40 degrees) and so the extent of the fusion (Lenke LG et al. J Bone Joint Surg Am 2001;83(8):1169-1181)

claims.name: at or above T6
claims.use: autonomic dysreflexia follows spinal cord injury at or above T6, so the injured level's side of the T6/T7 border sets the monitoring (Krassioukov A, Warburton DE, Teasell R, Eng JJ. Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2009;90(4):682-695; the level is in the review's background, not its abstract)

claims.name: below T12
claims.use: thoracic or lumbar: half of the spine surgeons surveyed reported operating at a wrong level at least once in their careers (Mody MG et al. Spine 2008;33(2):194-198), and the count from the lowest rib or the sacrum is the one a transitional column misleads

claims.name: below L2
claims.use: the interspace for a spinal needle: anaesthetists identified a marked lumbar interspace correctly in only 29 per cent of patients and placed it one space higher than they assumed in 51 per cent (Broadbent CR et al. Anaesthesia 2000;55:1122-1126), and the conus was damaged where spinal anaesthesia was given above the intended space (Reynolds F. Anaesthesia 2001;56:238-247)

claims.name: within the thoracolumbar junction, T11 to L2
claims.use: the junction of the rib-stiffened thoracic spine and the mobile lumbar spine; injuries of the thoracolumbar spine are classified and their treatment chosen by the Thoracolumbar Injury Classification and Severity Score (Vaccaro AR et al. Spine 2005;30(20):2325-2333)
